items.title: Transit Feasibility Study - Progress Report
notes: Report from C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services introduced Dennis Kar from Dillon Consulting and provided highlights of recent consultation activities.

Dennis Kar indicated the Township has commenced a Transit Feasibility Study (TFS) to identify a preferred transit solution that considers population and employment growth in the Township to the 2051 timeframe. He outlined the study objectives, the community engagement conducted to date, a progress report and the next steps in the project.

D. Kar responded to questions regarding the on-demand services and alignment with local services, opportunities to integrate with existing services such as Ride Well, phase II of the community engagement, expansion of the shuttle program, and future funding opportunities.

items.title: 2025 Water and Wastewater Rate Study and Financial Plans
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer introduced Daryl Abs, Managing Partner, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd.
Daryl Abs, Managing Partner, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd., provided an overview of the report and outlined the following recommendations:
· Minor increases to other rates (base charges, sprinkler systems, bulk water, etc.);
· Removing water and wastewater connection charges as of 2026; and · Requiring properties to connect to both water and wastewater systems.
Volume Rates
· Water Rates - 3.0% annual increase
· Wastewater Rates - 2.0% annual increase
· Blended Rate - 2.5% annual increase

Daryl Abs and Colin Baker responded to questions regarding requiring properties to connect to both water and wastewater systems, the ground water collection system in some neighbourhoods, and provided clarification regarding water rates average of 2% and sprinkler rates of 3%.
Councillor MacDonald requested consideration to reducing the wastewater rates from 2% to 1%.
Mayor Watters indicated there would be an opportunity during the budget deliberations to consider a reduction in the wastewater rates.

items.title: Community Engagement Charter and Strategy
notes: Report from K. Martin, Manager of Strategic Initiatives and Communications
K. Martin, Manager of Strategic Initiatives and Communications provided an overview of the report and introduced Tannis Topolnisky, Topent Ltd.

T. Topolnisky provided an outline of the project deliverables, including the Community Engagement Charter and Strategy, the action plan, the staff toolkit and templates. She outlined the engagement overview and the next steps in the process.

T. Topolnisky responded to questions regarding utilization of the feedback received rom the various advisory committees, mechanisms on providing follow up on the engagement, the use of exit surveys to gauge the engagement process, and staff time required to incorporate engagement into projects.
